title: Annotatio V §.IV: reply — organ defines mode; natural mouth makes Oral partly Natural/Capernaite
pass_a_gloss: REPLY. (1) That the organ of eating, most of all, makes for defining the mode of Eating; Seeing that Eating in the nominative case names an action through an organ or Instrument, one and another, by which it is performed, about to turn out modally diverse; So among the Lutherans themselves, Spiritual and Sacramental Eating import one and another mode of Eating, not so much from diversity of their Object or Foundation — which in each Eating, at least inadequately, is the same, namely Christ’s Body, to be eaten both Spiritually and Sacramentally or Oraliter in the Sacred Supper according to them — but from diversity of Organ, because Spiritual Eating of Christ’s Body is performed by the soul’s spiritual Mouth, i.e. by true living faith, and Sacramental conversely by the body’s corporal Mouth; Hence also the merely natural Organ by which the Eating of Christ’s Body called Supernatural is granted to be performed — namely the Body’s Natural mouth — so far indeed detracts from the Eating’s Supernaturality that it ought not to be called merely Supernatural, but also by just title Natural so far as it is instituted by the body’s natural Organ: But in the respect in which Eating is called Natural, in the same it also turns out Carnal and Capernaite, at least in part, because the Capernaites presumed Christ’s Body was to be eaten by the Body’s Mouth also; nay such arises from its chief part if not from the whole, because the Capernaites are nowhere read to have thrust into their Oral Eating of Christ’s body a tearing of teeth and casting of food into the Stomach more than the Lutherans themselves. Although each action, both Mastication of the teeth and Casting of the foodstuff into the stomach, essentially belongs to man’s Eating strictly so called Oral and having for Object solid food (such as Christ’s human body is), and the Author’s Instances prove nothing else — all wandering from the door and by the whole heaven. See above §. I.
pass_b_english: Reply (1): the organ most of all defines the mode. Even Lutherans distinguish spiritual from sacramental eating by organ — soul’s mouth (living faith) vs body’s mouth — not by a different object (Christ’s body in both).

A natural mouth so far makes the so-called supernatural eating also Natural, and thus partly Carnal/Capernaite. Strict oral eating of solid food (Christ’s human body) essentially includes chewing and stomach-descent — see §.I. The Author’s instances miss the door by a whole heaven.
source_text: RESPON. (1) Organon manducationis, omnium maximè, ad modum Manducationis definiendum, facere; Quandoquidem Manducatio in Casu recto actionem dicit per organum seu Instrumentum, aliud aliudque, quô peragitur, modaliter diversam evasuram; Ita ipsis Lutheranis, Spiritualis & Sacramentalis Manducatio, alium aliumque modum Manducationis inferunt, non adeo ob diversitatem sui Objecti, vel Fundamenti, quod in utraque Manducatione, saltem inadæquate, idem est, scil. Corpus Christi, & Spiritualiter, & Sacramentaliter, seu Oraliter, in S. Cœna, juxta ipsos, manducandum; sed ob diversitatem Organi, quòd Spiritualis Manducatio Corporis Christi, Ore animæ spirituali, h. e. fide verâ vivâque, Sacramentalis vice versâ, Ore Corporis corporali peragatur; Hinc etiam solum naturale Organon, quô Manducatio Corporis Christi, Supernaturalis dicta, conceditur peragi, puta os Corporis Naturale, Supernaturalitati Manducationis in tantum sanè detrahit, ut non merè Supernaturalis, sed justô etiam titulô, eatenus Naturalis dici debeat, quatenus Organô Corporis naturali instituitur: At, quô respectu Manducatio audit Naturalis, eodem & Carnalis, & Capernaitica, saltem ex parte evadit, quia Capernaitæ Corpus Christi Ore quoque Corporis præsumebant manducandum; quin talis, ex potissimâ sui parte, si non ex toto, enascitur, quia Capernaitæ Manducationi suæ Orali corporis Christi, nullibi Lacerationem dentium & dejectionem cibi in Ventriculum, magis quàm ipsi Lutherani intrusisse leguntur. Quanquam utraque actio, tàm Masticatio dentium, quàm Dejectio esculenti in ventriculum, ad Manducationem hominis stricte sic dictam Oralem, & pro Objecto solidum cibum, (qualis humanum Christi corpus est) habentem, essentialiter pertineat, nec Instantiæ Autoris aliud evincant, à janua omnes totôque cœlô aberrantes. Vide supra §. I.
notes: Organ defines mode; natural mouth → Capernaite.
